second_reasoning: The parent already supported keyboard argument completion, and its textarea selection handler refreshed only the skill menu, leaving the highlighted slash argument available for Tab. PR #122425 added a slash-menu refresh to that handler, routing an unchanged argument draft through the existing index reset.

I checked the stream feature and the option registration diffs: stream metadata edits already existed, and --on-exit-cwd was accepted only by cron add before PR #128373. The first version that accepted the flag on cron edit passed it to a resolver whose stream metadata branch returned before the existing validation, so the defect shipped with CLI support for that flag on edits.

OpenClaw already excluded Node 20 when #145688 introduced the shared resolver, but the resolver immediately served an existing subprocess launcher without checking the version floor. I checked that the later standalone probe retained the same acceptance rule and that the reported Gateway CI reproduction exercised it by placing Node 20 ahead of supported Node 24.

I checked the parent of #142713 and confirmed that the existing Access section rendered the inspection error and retry before checking for missing data. The tab refactor moved the error to a shared banner and left the permissions views showing a skeleton whenever inspection data was missing. The grouped settings editor, #150235, and the Solid port carried that behavior forward.

Local history shows that #181823 upgraded the bundle from 0.162.1 to 0.164.0 and that the pin stayed in place until this fix. The PR reports that native discovery uses the binary version and that 0.169.0 could see the newer models, which points to an upstream compatibility change. The separate relay fix restored catalog forwarding, and the PR's old-versus-new validator comparison confirms that the older schema rejected the newly introduced audio fileId format.

PR #199051 introduced the remembered Favorites tab with an explicit test requiring the picker to reopen on the selected model’s provider when that model was unstarred. The intervening favorites reorder kept that rule in place, and this fix changed the expected behavior in both the test and the documentation.

At the July 1 history boundary, NodeApp already retained a process-wide runtime and the camera manager already stored its lifecycle owner without clearing it on destruction. The September capture-isolation change added cancellation for active captures and left idle ownership as it was. The older path history stopped at a missing object, so I could not establish when the camera manager first began outliving its Activity.

Both original disclosure implementations compared newly allocated state objects by identity, and the later consolidation retained that check. The added test detects a synchronous unhide and rehide of closed disclosures, while the reported browser measurements show fewer style passes with the same disclosure behavior and no meaningful p95 improvement.

The migration diff shows that the previous file-backed compiler skipped writes when the existing cache contents matched. Moving the same cache to plugin state replaced that equality check with a fresh publication ID, a write, and deletion of the accepted predecessor even when the sources and output were unchanged. The fix's integration test checks publication ID, row metadata, and bytes across both warm and cold recompiles.

I checked the PostgreSQL reader port and its predecessor. The port added the PostgreSQL model-context branch with a JSONB cast on stored text, while the preceding projection used SQLite JSON functions. The later PostgreSQL optimization retained the same cast, and the separate full-text indexing port in #173462 bound message text directly into the PostgreSQL text column, causing the NUL write failure.

I checked the causing commit and its parent: the existing save handler wrote to the canonical workspace, and the parent resolved file reads against that same workspace after checkpointing. PR #194885 switched reads to the retained private checkout without checking whether the session was sandboxed and left the canonical write outside the checkpoint with no import back into that checkout. The fix adds coverage for both save-then-reload and host-only reads with a retained checkout.

The code before July 5 already sent a second live TwiML update after the greeting and used Gather without a timeout override or silence redirect. PR #100255 added automatic replies to webhook transcripts, which exposed the existing Gather behavior after those replies, while the September persistence refactor retained the separate listening update. Local history stops before the greeting sequence and Gather behavior were introduced, so I could not establish whether either had previously worked.

The original Visitor Access diff passed registration-time settings to the service and documented a Gateway restart after config edits, so those settings were designed to stay fixed for the life of the service. The #161267 diff added borrowing of live Gateway plugin instances by prepared agent runtimes, and its commit message explicitly records that a held turn can make replacement wait for the existing drain. I checked that the fix's parent still routed exclusive replacement through that drain, which is the path numeric limit edits now bypass.

The July 1 snapshot already truncated candidate lists before matching, and the September inventory refactor preserved that order. The offline history lookup stopped at a missing parent, so I could not verify whether the cap shipped with autocomplete or was added later.

Advisor's introduction already routed reviews through the Codex side-question handler, whose tool-policy, sandbox, and node-execution guards threw ordinary errors. The initial Advisor catch classified those errors as `fork_failed`, so the misleading warning shipped with the plugin.

The external-plugin preparation worker shipped with a synchronous source-root allocation on the Gateway thread, and the helper at that revision created directories and acquired the staging token synchronously. I checked that native-root allocation moved onto the host separately in #177067 and that the model-catalog pool already used synchronous directory creation, so the cited commit accounts for the external-plugin source path within a fix that covers several paths.

The early-listener commit introduced both the interval in which HTTP could accept requests before runtime readiness and the wait that blocked Control UI documents and assets during that interval. I verified that the wait remained ahead of Control UI routing immediately before the fix and that the new HTTP test requires the app and assets to load while the readiness promise is still pending. The Solid migration carried forward the earlier cold-start sign-in logic, so the cause here is the fresh-visit startup failure.

The invitation authority already returned `limit_reached` for both invitation count and lifetime limits before the Access page was introduced. The introducing diff routed access action failures through `peopleError` and gave that shared code a single people-or-devices message, so invitation limit refusals received misleading guidance from the first version of the page.

I checked the introducing diff, which added the failure-detail renderer and wired it into the progress cards in the same commit. The renderer used a raw slice from its first version, and the fix’s browser evidence reproduced the broken glyph for both parent and child failures.

I checked that the adapter already requested window state without a format before the upgrade and that an earlier live Linux X11 proof required usable element references. The fix PR reproduced missing references on CUA 0.37 and restored them by requesting structured elements explicitly. The available evidence did not include a live result from the immediate parent on CUA 0.36.

The causing diff introduced the account-wide flood gate and its synthetic 429 for typing attempts made during an active wait. The parent revision already wrapped typing calls in an error logger with no filter at that call site, so the misleading ERROR shipped with the new skip behavior.

The parent-side diff shows that discovery already ran the same Claude login check through `spawnSync`, so caller cancellation could not interrupt a refresh in progress. The causing commit wired cancellation into the process runner, and I verified that the runner already terminated the process tree on abort with a 300 ms grace period. The fix PR reproduced the resulting orphaned lock and delay with the real Claude CLI.

The oldest readable version already printed “Manual OAuth entry required” while the browser callback could still complete sign-in. The October refactor removed an immediate fallback branch, but its parent set the flag that bypassed that branch whenever it announced browser sign-in, even after a bind failure. The offline history ends before the misleading wording was introduced, so I could not verify its introducing diff or establish that either symptom was a regression.

The parent commit already supported non-English Control UI locales. The introducing diff added the saved onboarding greeting with English-only text and gave the model an English role question without a locale instruction. The greeting helper's path history shows that its English-only implementation persisted until this fix.

The original lazy playback implementation in #115987 already routed QuickTime files through the transcode path, encoded video with libx264, and returned a pending result while encoding ran. The original chat video player in #116115 already polled for readiness and displayed the preparation message during the first check. The patch optimizes that existing playback flow, and the reported speedup comes from a synthetic replay against the deployed baseline.

I checked the parent and confirmed that the existing Codex model-context reader loaded all entries selected by the compaction boundary without a byte limit. PR #149520 added the token-derived cap and a test that expected older turns to be dropped, and PR #159375 later moved the same cap into the shared helper used by Agents API.

The parent used injected startup credentials, and #159860 introduced the native challenge bridge, the window-lifetime authorization check, and retryable handling of WebKit bridge refusals together. I checked the controller at that commit and confirmed that close and replacement still only called `webView.stopLoading()`, which left the committed document alive to retry after a disconnect.

I checked the parent of #178764 and confirmed that existing custom session targets ran through the isolated cron runner, whose catch block returned the normalized exception text. The migration routed those jobs through a receipt that could fall back to generic text even when the reply operation held the original exception. The source establishes the loss of detail at that boundary, but the exact account-binding failure was only demonstrated in the fix’s evidence.

I checked the cold-storage introduction and the updater at that revision: file-backed archives depended on payloads under the store's cold directory, while rehearsal copied the agent databases without those files. Rehearsal therefore produced incomplete snapshots for file-backed archives from their introduction. The reported candidate revision was unavailable locally, and the evidence bundle does not identify which Doctor repair selected the reporter's archive.

I checked the parent of #191978 and confirmed that session events already scheduled a refresh that cleared the current error and entered the loading state. The #191978 diff introduced a persistent FORBIDDEN response for guests opening someone else’s Activity, exposing that existing refresh behavior when an unrelated session changed.

I checked the completion renderer’s introduction in #198133 and the transcript avatar rollout in #201407. The completion renderer already used a generic robot, and the rollout added colored avatars to launch rows while leaving the completion renderer untouched, so avatar continuity was missing from the first version of transcript avatars.

The parent of #133683 already emitted startup span-end events, and the awaited HTTP-listen span was written synchronously before dispatch readiness. #133683 introduced the write delay, and #188873 later moved sidecar readiness after post-attach span completion while leaving the flush deferred. The local history establishes the ordering change, but I could not verify when the affected collector began taking its snapshot at `/readyz`.

I checked that the parent of #153542 already supported image-only MCP results. The original recovery sidebar added in #153542 treated missing text as missing output even for a completed match, and the later Solid refactors carried that check forward.

The July adoption implementation added `sandbox list --limit ... --offset ...` while the E2E workflow pinned OpenShell v0.0.92. The October dependency refresh changed the workflow pin from v0.1.2 to v0.1.3 without changing the backend, and the fix PR reproduced the rejected `--limit` flag on that pinned release. The evidence supports an upstream CLI contract change exposed by the pin update, though the older CLI behavior could not be independently verified offline.

The introducing diff added saved operator authority for scheduled continuations and routed each occurrence through the existing exact-generation check. At that commit, trusted-proxy sessions already saved a generation that hashed required headers, so changing those headers could invalidate a saved automation even while the creator’s grant remained valid. The Enterprise upgrade exposed the same failure by changing the rendered proxy configuration.

The introducing diff added the source-lifecycle guard and a test that expected the announcement to report success even though the gateway never ran and a frozen result was available. A later commit gave that same refusal the explicit `intentional_non_delivery` disposition, and the subsequent saved-result notice change left the refusal outside the failure path.

The parent of #106513 already advertised up to ten images and one movie while loading at most three images and no video attachments. I checked that #106513 added the Send block for omitted items, turning an existing mismatch into a disabled Send button. The offline history ends before the mismatch can be traced to its introduction, so I could not establish whether those selections had ever been fully supported.

The introducing diff adds the updater-exit recovery branch and the standalone repair restoration phase, with all three defects present in their first implementation. The new helper skipped the stop check when restoration was already armed and never rechecked it before startup, while the new standalone phase turned a non-owned service verdict into an error after repair. Candidate identity was verified before finalization, but the terminal writer switched only after recovery returned, so a repair that changed the schema and then failed left the staged writer selected.

The parent diff shows that command checkpoints already synchronized directly to the canonical workspace before #196662 added btrfs snapshot creation and removal. Later commits narrowed when snapshots ran and allowed the guest to keep running during capture, but large changed workspaces still incurred the filesystem transaction and cleanup costs. The fix PR reports production Gateway stalls and verifies the elimination of snapshot and removal requests in an APFS fixture with simulated btrfs eligibility.

The parent of #132090 already dispatched yielded child batches and returned no explicit resolver for mixed bindings, allowing delivery when a live Gateway request scope was available. #132090 made a mixed batch carry an explicit rejecting resolver, and #137606 later made the same bound-and-unbound mismatch throw before dispatch. The earlier fallback is visible in the code, while successful delivery after restoration before #132090 is unverified.

Before #159860, the shared-credential auth value compared during reconnect contained only the Gateway URL, token, and password, so unchanged settings kept the existing WebView and its offline queue. The introducing diff made that same comparison sensitive to socket-owned credentials, so retirement before reconnect made otherwise identical configurations compare unequal and caused the dashboard to replace the WebView.

I checked the original portable engine diff and its subsequent path history: the first implementation already rejected whole replies when a list exceeded its schema limit and returned a partial result on validation failure. The fix PR reports a live run that recovered seven findings after the change, and its added test covers overlong planning, extraction, and audit lists. The side-panel-only change addresses a separate UI decision.

The parent-side diff shows that compressed archive reads invoked an age-based sweep that deleted entries older than 24 hours. PR #193548 switched readers to streaming and removed the sweep, so existing cache files lost their automatic cleanup path. The fix PR reports that a real Doctor repair on the baseline left a seeded cache file in place.

The causing diff introduced the configured-MCP loopback bridge with senderless acquisition, and the runtime manager only materialized requester-scoped servers when given a sender. I checked the preceding native CLI path, which also acquired its policy catalog without a requester and dropped servers with no allowed tools. The omission therefore shipped with the bridge.

The fix's test exercises a child launched with only OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, and the pre-fix launcher passed that environment through without carrying the parent's SQLite selection. I checked the bundled Bun rollout, the switch to asynchronous credential reads in setup, and the subprocess launch history, but could not establish which change first exposed the failure or verify a previously working bundled Bun setup.

#153989 introduced live operator authority for queued follow-ups, consumed input on any assertion exception, and latched revocation found by a direct check without aborting the signal. #198245 made policy evaluation errors recoverable at the authority layer, while the follow-up runner still consumed the message. #200213 surfaced that existing discard as a withheld failure.

I checked the commit that introduced operator run authority and confirmed that both errors lacked recovery guidance from the start. The fix changes the error text, and the PR reports that fresh authenticated requests already succeeded after revocation on the baseline. The revocation that triggered the reported incident remains unattributed.

The parent of #169773 already computed fallback recovery from the admitted session model and cleared the saved notice, and its existing tests expected a recovery notice in direct chats. I checked the introducing diff and confirmed that its new guard canceled the existing state transition when the response model differed from the selected model, which can happen when a separate finalizer writes the reply.

I checked the commit that added the guard and confirmed that the 47,500-entry threshold deliberately leaves room below the 50,000-entry cap in shipped updaters. The PR measurements show that cumulative growth in runtime output, Control UI assets, and extensions pushed the package over the guard while it remained below the shipped cap. The measured commits were unavailable locally, so I could not verify a specific trigger commit.

The commit that introduced gallery navigation already loaded attachments by URL and discarded the decoded Image, leaving revisits dependent on browser cache state. I checked that the Gateway served mutable media without validators before gallery navigation shipped and that later gallery refactors preserved the same decode-and-return behavior.

Before #121113, cleanup already captured cancellation before awaiting cleanup lock acquisition, which itself drained transcript work, and the idle helper raced only agent idle against a timeout. #121113 replaced lock acquisition with the transcript drain at the same point, and #146842 changed how pending writes were flushed while preserving the idle race. The idle helper predates the shallow boundary, and the available offline history could not establish its introducing diff or an earlier working cancellation path.

I verified that the fix's parent used the 1.5-second fallback for servers without an explicit request timeout. The fix description attributes the cap to PR #85063, but the local path history stopped at the July 1 graft because an older object was missing. I could not inspect that PR's diff or verify whether slow listings had worked before it.

The parent already recorded ClawHub installs as `source: "clawhub"` and linked them to the host during installation, while Doctor's existing repair scanned only managed npm roots. PR #118304 introduced Doctor's repair for registered installs under the extensions root, and its npm-only filter excluded ClawHub records from the start.

The watcher already stopped respawning on a detected bind conflict before the July 1 history boundary, and the July bind-detection fix retained that policy while making it more reliable. The fix description links the policy to #65042, but the available offline history could not verify that commit's diff or establish whether transient conflicts recovered before it.

Before #153063, ordinary status probed the selected Gateway directly with a 2.5-second default probe timeout and did not wait on a LaunchAgent. #153063 put a 60-second readiness budget on that path, and the waiter's early exit for a free port required a stopped runtime, so an unknown runtime could consume the budget. The later absent-Gateway fix added a strict command read and a native-runtime fallback, preserving the long wait when the unrelated LaunchAgent prevented a missing-unit verdict.

The operator-role launch created the mismatch by restricting session creation and runs while the existing picker continued to consume an unfiltered `agents.list` response. I checked the roster handler before and at the role launch and verified that the later catalog refactor and model-policy changes carried the unfiltered roster forward.

The introducing diff shows that Doctor previously only reported legacy captures and that automatic cleanup shipped with a census that vetoed deletion whenever the Darwin reader threw. The initial reader rejected unreadable foreign processes such as third-party daemons and Apple app services, and I verified that #157102 retained that restriction. The host-wide census was extended to managed native cleanup later in #158414.

The first-parent history and introducing diff show that PR #175256 added both the host-side bounded seed capability and the unguarded observer call. The same diff shows Codex awaiting the capability to build the fresh thread's history, so the observer failure could abort this path from its first release.

The initial local managed-workspace projection captured guest-created files, including ignored files, and sent them through the existing 64 MiB per-file result limit. I checked the exclusions and result validator at that commit and confirmed that an oversized scratch file could enter the result from the first version. The later blame candidate added exclusions for test caches and build locks, leaving scratch handling as it was.

I checked the introducing diff: #133037 replaced package-based setup with a Gateway-served runtime download, gave the request and its transfer grant ten-minute limits, and put the new download inside the existing fifteen-minute enrollment command. Later fixes added retries, resume, and a longer transfer grant, which exposed the command deadline in the reported run. Slow transfers that needed more than the fixed budgets had been unsupported since this download path shipped.

I checked the causing commit and its parent: previously, a thrown commit error closed the socket with a retryable reason, and the worker resubmitted the same request after reconnecting. The causing commit turned those interruptions into cached terminal rejections, and the fix adds a regression test covering transient errors and a lost SQLite commit receipt.

I checked the feature’s introducing diff and confirmed that its first version already awaited asynchronous model preparation before starting the generation timer. The path history and the fix’s parent-side diff show that the same ordering persisted after the narration code was split and utility completion routing changed.

The introducing diff extends gateway-wide management from authenticated Control UI administrators to configured channel owners. At that commit, the ingress wrapper already revoked its capability when the immediate call settled, and the existing queue drained later without recreating that capability for the new run. Queued owner messages therefore lacked gateway-wide management from the first version of the feature.

The generic Gateway timeout formatter predates the July 1 history boundary and described the client deadline without addressing the write outcome. PR #126743 narrowed offline fallback to pre-connect failures and missing credentials, so the agent deletion command began surfacing the existing timeout directly when a dispatched write went unconfirmed. The fix report reproduced that path by withholding the successful reply and confirming that the agent was gone.

The history RPCs already existed before #138917, and I checked that their cold reads opened the existing database directly without preparing a snapshot. The #138917 diff routed both RPCs through synchronous snapshot preparation, adding the blocking work that the fix’s authenticated RPC test targets.

I checked the introducing diff and its parent: the parent already rejected explicit task-suggestion mode mismatches, and #177698 added the prepared same-requester join without exempting it from that comparison. The older blame candidate explains where the explicit setting came from, but the incompatible setting was already present when the prepared join shipped. The fix bundle reproduces the failure on the later main revision, and the origin at #177698 is inferred from the source.

I checked the introducing diff and confirmed that the fatal renewal path discarded the caught error from the first version of the heartbeat worker. The fix sends that error to the host before teardown, and the PR reports that the original CI heartbeat failure remained unreproduced.

The release gate uses SSE, and #122194 introduced stateful SSE continuation by reusing the provider’s terminal output. Its parent already dropped `content: []` from the saved signature and kept ciphertext from the item-done event when present, so the mismatch was possible from the first stateful SSE version. The fix’s fixture confirms the mechanism with synthetic payloads, and the provider’s payloads at the time of introduction were unavailable.

The first federated Codex catalog already paired 30-second UI polling with native thread/list discovery, and the fix's parent still called native discovery when its page cache needed refreshing. The PR's benchmark measures the benefit of bypassing that recurring work, and the checked history does not establish a previously faster baseline for the recurring polling behavior this change targets.

I checked the September SQLite admission change and the October fix diff, which documents the eMudhra key compromise. The earlier check addressed SQLite compatibility, while the external compromise made previously trusted keys unsafe in the admitted Node runtimes and the native pnpm TLS runtime.

Before the migration, the Lit panel kept tab content mounted by tab ID, and its boolean attribute binding left the disclosure alone when the expansion preference stayed the same. I checked the migration diff and its parent, where the existing GitHub panel end-to-end test already asserted that an opened file diff stayed open after switching tabs and returning. The Solid migration made the file's open binding react to tab revisions even when the expansion preference was unchanged.

The parent of #151470 still rendered subagent rows in the sidebar, and #151470 introduced the documented workflow of inspecting hidden runs in chat from an ancestor's warning. Its sidebar diff retained the warning, while the chat notice renderer at that revision only handled the current chat's run error and had no child attention input. The fix's browser reproduction confirms the missing notice on its baseline when no new parent reply carries the child's diagnostic.

PR #124613 introduced blocked-submit feedback and covered a single preference restore, but its diff tied the notice to the first blocking check from day one. The fix parent still used that same comparison, and PR #127823 separately introduced the exception that kept Start natively enabled when a blocking reason existed. The history explains why feedback could disappear when checks changed, but does not establish why every reported attempt lacked a visible notice.

The original broker already rejected opens when `this.clients.size >= MAX_STORES`, and the first shared-state worker cache retained idle handles without a way to release them under admission pressure. I checked the original broker and cache diffs and confirmed that the later idle timeout changes only affected how long handles stayed cached.

The oldest readable snapshot already shows the macOS prompter accepting only requested events and waiting for each prompt inline, even though the Gateway published exec.approval.resolved. The later timeout and connection-ownership changes retained that behavior. The full-history path lookup stopped at a missing parent, so I could not verify the introducing diff or establish whether cross-client dismissal ever worked.

The baseline update completed successfully, and the fix shortens its outage by moving advisory work after readiness. I checked the September restart changes and found that fresh Doctor already ran before a restart, including when plugin changes required a separate stop and restart.

I checked the worker runtime and launch descriptor in their introducing commit, which hard-coded full execution and had no field for the Gateway's exec policy. The later tool-authority change sent allowed tool names only, and subsequent session-permission changes still did not carry the resolved exec policy.

I checked the parent of #107295 and confirmed that the bundled QQ Bot contract used `collectConditionalChannelFieldAssignments`, which attached account owners to active root and named SecretRefs. The Tencent package migration removed that contract and shipped a host fallback whose assignments defaulted to `ownerKind: "unknown"`. The existing resolver rethrew missing-secret errors for unknown owners even when account isolation was enabled.

I checked the introducing diff and its parent, where Markdown highlighted code inline. The first worker implementation tied cancellation to viewport intersection and pane lifecycle, leaving no path for tab hiding to release a pending worker. The owner and worker files were unchanged between that introduction and the fix.

The introducing diff added explicit object repair with a five-minute deadline and a repository-wide scan that had to finish before any fetch. The path history shows that this scan and deadline stayed in place until the resumability fix, so the starvation case existed from the first version of explicit repair.

I checked the causing commit's parent and confirmed that Doctor already used verified snapshots, whose publisher copied the image into staging and checked its fingerprint before hard-link publication. PR #162403 replaced that copy for owned snapshot images with a transfer that checks the fingerprint after unlinking a name, which rejects an unchanged inode when Node reports ctime as birth time.

The diff for 8d4e374169be shows the production plugin entry point switching from VoiceCallConfigSchema.parse to normalizeVoiceCallConfig. That left the export in use only by tests and fixtures, which triggered a production dead-code check while Voice Call behavior stayed the same.

I traced the two-reference design to #119594, which added `releaseQueuedFollowupWorkAdmission = retainGatewayWorkAdmission()` and released the queue reference in `onSettled`. The immediately preceding patch, #164181, added a release on abort for the queue reference alone, leaving the source reference with the waiting dispatch. The diffs establish the ownership gap, but I could not verify when it first began blocking the preceding turn.

I checked the refactor’s diff and its parent manifest, which already referenced the existing Control UI assets under `e57c147e…`. The fix PR reports that the earlier source produced that hash and that the changed source produced `df3cf5b4…`, explaining the validation and Docker package preparation failures.

The introducing diff shows that agent databases and session transcripts used SQLite before #173462 first enabled PostgreSQL for them. At that commit, archive persistence still called `ensureSessionTranscriptArchiveSchema(database.db)`, whose installer explicitly rejected PostgreSQL, and the new PostgreSQL lifecycle test disabled archival.

The parent of #159873 used generic run admission and issued no scheduled message capability for the script. I checked that the creator-origin check already existed when #159873 introduced the script’s message grant with an origin-free policy. #176158 later restored the origin during preparation and included it in the cache key, but admission still used the original request policy.

PR #128905 introduced commit-status reporting and placed the notification after the prepared write returned. I checked the deletion wrapper and harness owner code at that commit and confirmed that the owner path could still throw after the database write committed, so the reporting defect was present when the feature shipped.

I checked that the bundled-plugin test already rejected manifests whose category count was anything other than one. The Search API commit's diff shows that DeepSeek previously met that requirement with a single `models` category and began failing it when the commit added `web`.

The parent of #124301 already had composer run-status feedback and a transcript render guard whose dependencies excluded run status. #124301 added phase and timestamp to the shared guard, causing even a status change that left every message unchanged to rerender settled rows. #127823 moved the interruption row back to the composer and left both dependencies in place.

PR #136329 replaced the existing npm backup move helper with `await fs.rename(targetSwapRoot, backupRoot)`, which aborts the swap on the first rename error. I checked the parent call site and its recovery tests, which establish a copy fallback for cross-device moves but leave the earlier helper's behavior under transient Windows locks unverified.

The header introduced in #122335 used the pane’s session list to resolve the child’s parent key, and the Gateway tests immediately before #150196 asserted that authorized lists included Incognito sessions and that Incognito children retained their parent keys. #150196 switched `sessions.list` to a projection that excludes Incognito rows and reversed the list assertion, so a refresh left the header without the parent row even though the lineage still existed.

The old helper checked only the final component for an existing directory and scoped creation to the nearest existing ancestor, which could leave a symlinked parent outside validation. The fix also documents that pathScope trims its input, explaining the changed directory name. The helper predates the shallow boundary, and the older path history hit a missing object, so I could not verify when either failure began.

The parent of #147711 could archive orphans during ordinary imports, and #147711 introduced the deferred receipt and settlement path with the incomplete source inventory. I checked that #149308 broadened receipt eligibility to imports with missing-transcript warnings, while the fix's evidence shows the omission also affected imports without those warnings.

The scenario began verifying settled replies with this commit, and I checked that the runtime already supported appending context and system-prompt metadata before the assistant replied. The later verbatim-result change preserved the ancestry check, and the fix’s metadata fixture directly exercises the missing link in the original verifier.

The parent already supported explicit `plugins.reload`, and its lifecycle test expected the request to succeed after a config write. The parent's metadata lookup was synchronous between transaction checkpoints, so a watcher callback could not interleave at that point. PR #154792 introduced that interleaving, and the fix's test injects the watcher event there to reproduce the false rejection.

I checked the parent of #148624 and confirmed that the account name was already clipped by CSS and carried the full name in a native tooltip. The removal caused the account hover regression, and the fix also adds a reveal interaction to agent and workspace labels that already clipped long names.

The original Storage settings feature used a PollController whose timer called its callback regardless of tab visibility. I checked that the later visibility-aware controller defaulted to always polling and that Storage settings still used that default immediately before the Solid migration carried the same behavior forward with a raw interval.

I checked the first-parent sidebar history and the introducing diff. Adopted rows already used the regular session renderer when the native catalog menu was added, and the new menu handlers were reachable only on rows without a matching live session. The native menu therefore never worked on adopted rows.

The prior main commit pinned fs-safe 0.12.0 and documented that guarded JavaScript paths supported normal filesystem operations with the native helper off on macOS and Linux. The 0.13 adoption exposed that longstanding default because atomic no-clobber moves now require the native helper, and the fix's compiled-package tests verify the refusal with native mode off. The dependency upgrade and the compatibility changes landed together.

I checked the preceding stylesheet and confirmed that each row defined its own grid, with the 20px avatar track and 8px gap starting inside the row padding. The causing diff moved the fixed track to the shared list grid, where the padded row inherited it and lost the gap. The fix restores that spacing and also adjusts vertical alignment on touch devices.

The diff for #129423 introduced the prepared-range fallback with the slice before projection, so it could lose the marker from its first release. The preceding fallback already read the raw branch across prior compactions, and the fix's test shows how a tool-only preparation with an earlier cut sent the already-compacted user message to the summarizer.

The introducing commit stored invitation deadlines but implemented expiry and revocation through Cloudflare policy cleanup, leaving open Gateway connections and accepted runs independent of the grant. The later invitation-validation change checked guest roles and administrator authority when managing invitations, and the fix's Gateway diff shows where grant checks and cancellation were first added to request dispatch.

The shared UI filter already used `!row.spawnedBy` to keep child rows out of the top-level session inventory, and #126388 exposed the gap by promoting categorized children into sidebar groups while leaving that filter in place. I checked that the palette already used the exclusion for title and transcript search before #152314 moved those filters to the Gateway, where the same exclusion continued.

The July 1 snapshot already logged the same status-only INFO completion entry for results that could carry an error reason. PR #128868 introduced the upstream-mismatch refusal used in the fix's reproduction and left the completion logger alone. The available path history stops at the shallow boundary, so I could not establish when the general logging defect began or whether an earlier version logged those reasons.

I checked the original latch, which explicitly excluded Codex, and confirmed that native compaction counts already flowed through shared session accounting before #136533. When #136533 extended the latch to Codex sessions, that accounting path could immediately erase a matching latch without changing the host transcript. The defect therefore shipped with Codex support for the latch.

I checked the original Inbox diff, which explicitly required broad operator read access before session-only grants existed. PR #155184 expanded scoped conversation access and switched the documented guest role from broad grants to session-only grants while retaining the Inbox gates. PR #178038 later enabled guest sending and lookup while explicitly retaining the broad-read requirement for Inbox RPCs.

The July cancellation refactor replaced `new Error(`${method} aborted`)` with a typed wrapper that still omitted the signal reason, and the earlier startup request had its own timeout that could report `turn/start timed out`. PR #134755 added an execution deadline that could expire while `turn/start` was pending and called `runAbortController.abort(error)`, exposing the existing wrapper's loss of the deadline explanation.

The landed product diff changes the dashboard CLI, while the subagent recovery implementation referenced in the PR description landed separately in #176861. The introducing diff for `dashboard --json` already sent failures only to stdout, which the runtime implementation confirms. The later blame candidate #168812 changed the JSON envelope and left stderr behavior as it was.

The causing commit’s parent admitted an existing Gateway owner using PID and process start time without requiring a namespace probe. The causing diff placed namespace verification ahead of those checks, so PRoot’s `stat` failure turned the Gateway’s own fresh owner into an unknown owner and caused admission to throw, matching the fix PR’s live reproduction.

The existing startup check had a recorded passing baseline of 362,012 gzip bytes under the 362,588-byte limit. I verified that #149287 added preview copy to the eager catalog and #150491 subsequently deferred it, but the offline evidence does not establish the exact startup size immediately before and after #149287. The separate cold-worktree fixture repair had already landed before this commit.

I checked the introducing diff and confirmed that it added the read operation and a tool that passed paths directly to the delimiter-splitting reader, so that tool could never resolve these keys. A later commit expanded command validation to accept quoted and escaped paths, exposing the same lookup failure through typed commands.

The July 1 checkout snapshot already used lowercase substring matching in sessions.files.list, which misses canonically equivalent filenames in different Unicode forms. The September extraction into workspace-files.ts and the later refactors preserved that comparison. Offline history stops at the shallow boundary, so I could not verify whether the first implementation shipped with this defect or an older change introduced it.

The shared JSON failure contract shipped in #124849 with this gap. I checked that commit's diff and source: both commands already caught their own flag errors, and the shared mutation handler wrote JSON only when `params.options.dryRun && params.options.json` was true, so these errors never reached the new top-level JSON formatter.

I checked the causing commit and its parent. The parent already claimed the writer after admission and read the current session row during native setup, and the fix PR reports a passing pre-change baseline and a bisect to #168992. That commit made the first ownership check use the pre-claim snapshot, so its writer ID failed the existing check.

The reported failures were confined to the CI wrapper-shadowing guard and unused-export scans. I checked that #173327 added an SDK wrapper that delegated through an aliased import and that #174217 removed the transport redactor's call as part of an intentional logging change.

I classified the fix by its default-agent failure: before #114388, bind and unbind called a resolver that honored the roster's `default: true` marker. That commit moved the marker to `systemAgent.agentId` during migration and left both commands using a resolver that ignores the new field, while #146246 restored default selection elsewhere. The account-casing mismatch and partial-add success status were already present in the oldest local snapshot, and their introducing diffs were unavailable offline.

I checked the causing commit's parent and confirmed that the Node installer already preserved `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and delegated lifecycle actions to the shared service adapter, whose mutation guard only refused externally supervised services. PR #115922 added the default-install identity check to that shared guard, so an existing custom state directory began blocking Node commands before they reached the native service manager.

The PR reports CPU savings on synthetic workloads and matching results for cleanup, search, and replay. The replay query already counted every session before #139982 moved it to a prepared query, and #147166 introduced exact-session search with the existing unscoped dirty-state lookup. The evidence supports a performance improvement to existing behavior.

I checked the causing commit’s parent and confirmed that Gateway cron already used the prepared inbound loader, which could reuse a compatible process-active registry without a request scope. PR #161267 made that lookup depend on a scoped registry, so detached condition checks fell back to loading plugins already registered at startup. The fix PR’s restart evidence shows that duplicate registration exhausted the 30-second evaluation budget.

I checked that the parent commit displayed per-category operation counts alongside the failure count and that those counts included failed calls. The causing diff replaced the operation counts with a duration heading while retaining failure badges, removing the context that the fix restores as a single total.

I checked that #132610 made `execFile("ps", …)` part of mandatory Codex startup registration, where it worked on hosts that allowed `ps`. The documented failure occurs in the signed standalone Bun deployment added by #172384 when Seatbelt denies that executable. I also checked #169628, whose initial automatic setup loop continued to the next candidate after a Codex activation error, explaining the separate Ollama fallback symptom.

The #162175 diff introduced selected-provider health reporting in `memory status` and passed unresolved configuration to the provider from the first implementation. Path history shows that #162176 subsequently introduced Doctor’s provider-runtime probe with the same omission.

The Groq manifest history shows that #113681 introduced the Qwen 3.6 row with the incorrect image flag, and the Cohere diff independently shows that #102489 introduced North Mini Code with the same incorrect flag. The Groq refresh also updated a reasoning compatibility helper, and a later cleanup removed it after it became unreferenced. The evidence does not establish when enabled reasoning first failed on the Gateway path, so the cited cause is the verified Groq image capability defect.

The September refactor moved the existing `beast` default into the shared resolver, and the October refactor preserved that default when it moved option resolution into session creation. The previous documentation specified `beast`, and the PR reports successful captures on smaller machines without identifying a failure on `beast`, so this was a change in resource allocation policy.

The introducing diff added the scanner with whole-plist JSON conversion and a 1 MiB output limit, making identifier lookup depend on unrelated metadata from the first release. First-parent history shows no intervening changes to the scanner, and the fix PR reports reproducing the missing identifier with a native date fixture against the original reader.

The introducing commit added the personal skills library CLI with unsanitized metadata interpolation already in place. I checked that its library store used the profile display name directly as the owner label and that the CLI passed formatted output to the stdout writer.

The PR explicitly calls this a requested policy change, and the prior multi-user guide documented archive and restore access for write operators on sessions they created or were assigned to. The pre-fix Gateway applied its general session mutation policy to archive and restore, and the fix added a creator-or-admin requirement specific to those operations.

The oldest readable implementation already read the summary and then called `fs.writeFile(outputPath, body, "utf8")` without checking whether the paths identified the same file, so the defect predates the later evidence-report feature. The available path history could not reach the introducing diff before the July 1 shallow boundary, leaving it unclear whether the defect shipped with summary reporting or appeared in an earlier regression.

PR #135865 introduced the workspace conflict callout as a plain `<div class="callout danger">` and carried forward an ordinary save-error callout that already lacked alert semantics. The later rendering refactors preserved that omission, and the ordinary error callout predates the shallow history boundary, so the available diffs establish the origin of the conflict branch only.

The introducing diff added both failure paths with the unified rail snapshot, after sidebar pagination and the owner-first window already existed. I checked the previous cache reader, which also rejected rosters above 200 rows, and confirmed that the later validation refactor carried the same cap into the new schema file.

The July 1 snapshot already lowercased the query and skill text before calling `.includes()` without Unicode normalization. The later UI moves and caching changes preserved that comparison. The offline history lookup failed on a missing pre-graft commit, so I could not verify whether the original filter shipped with this behavior or an earlier change introduced it.

I checked #180466's loader and documentation diff, which shows that edited bundled code previously required a Gateway restart and that the same commit introduced live reload and the capture early return. The parent loader could redirect shared imports, but native Workers did not inherit its hooks, so the new reload path shipped with missing relative module targets. The fix's Worker test exercises that path through reload and recovery.

The Knowledge plugin landed on main with both the mobile flex row and the four-row loading placeholder. The introducing diff styles the placeholder blocks as a grid with a 44px minimum height per row, so the stack sets the flex row's height and stretches the Everything chip. The only intervening change across the stylesheet and Browse renderer converted an import to a type-only import.

I checked the parent code and confirmed that first AWS captures already used `--wait`, accepted a successful response without an attestation, and published the image before enrollment. The diff for #171729 switched eligible captures to `--wait=false` and required an attestation that the fix PR confirms Crabbox 0.78.0 never returned, breaking the existing capture and enrollment flow on main.

The introducing commit added the relay submission paths and the fixed 15-second signal together. I checked that the Gateway ingress at that commit already combined the request signal with the principal signal and passed it into run authority, so the original relay could cancel accepted work when the submission deadline expired.

The introducing diff added the scrollable picker with Material 3's default sheet gestures, and first-parent history shows the picker file stayed unchanged until the fix. The fix PR reproduced dismissal through Material's gesture handler, but its reproduction used a revision after an intervening Compose BOM update, so launch-version behavior remains unverified.

The original implementation used rollback as the native cause, and #141477 deliberately switched to the initiating failure while retaining both errors in AggregateError.errors. The previous tests explicitly asserted that choice, and the fix preserves the messages, diagnostic order, and redaction. The evidence shows an internal error-contract change and lint cleanup without a reported failure.

The introducing diff added the paired-node Memory and Skills worker launch with the workspace as its working directory, and the runtime helper at that revision loaded `tsx` without an explicit configuration path. The same commit added a test mock that supplied the checkout configuration for children running outside the checkout, showing that the production path shipped with the defect.

The first-parent history shows that #146267 introduced TLS renewal before #146275, and the pre-refactor owner spread the caller's array into its registry and invoked the renewal handle's `stop()` during shutdown. #146275 switched the same registration path to variadic arguments while leaving the TLS caller unchanged, causing the shutdown code to call `stop()` on an array.

The introducing diff shows that catalog lookup and terminal creation previously ran without the shared 30-second Gateway deadline. PR #107688 introduced that deadline with wall-clock arithmetic, and first-parent path history confirms that the later helper extraction carried the same arithmetic forward.

The existing reader deliberately rejected newer schemas, and the schema bump from 17 to 18 exposed the limits of the generic open warning when the Gateway and companion worker ran different versions. I verified the schema bump and the pre-existing check on reused read handles, and the fix preserves that check while adding diagnostics. The PR reproduced the old reader’s refusal in isolation, but the reporter’s exact process and nested error were never captured.

Both flags already used the trimming helper at the July 1 shallow boundary, and the later Docker cleanup carried both calls forward unchanged. The offline history stops at that boundary because its parent object is missing, so I could not determine whether the flags shipped with trimming or acquired it later.

The candidate-admission change introduced a preflight that invoked the ancestry guard without a run ID, even though the existing lease verifier required one. I checked that the older execution path passed `updateRun: opts.run` and that #158314 retained the same run ID lookup, so the affected candidate inspection shipped with the defect.

The PR reports two unused-export findings from the scheduled production Knip check. The fix diff confirms that every change is to a type declaration, type import, or fixture type annotation, so the fix addresses a tooling finding.

I checked that #119729 added timestamp recovery for chat abort controllers and that #123189 extended it to owners in the embedded-run registry. #126566 first registered deferred CLI owners in that registry without a start timestamp, so the new recovery path fell back to the current time from its first version.

The earlier agent-update tests explicitly expected the queued notice, and the restart recovery history shows that the heading already had a summary before its latest wording change. The fix changes which status text the transcript displays, and the PR describes redundant copy without reporting a delivery or recovery failure.

I checked the causing commit's parent and confirmed that the local CLI already supported `--session-id` and that its worker listing returned an empty result for a schema-less store, allowing dispatch to continue. The new exact-entry lookup throws on `schema-missing`, which matches the local failure reported in the fix's negative control.

The commit message attributes the findings to the CI dependency check. The full diff confirms that the changes are limited to removing unused exports and teaching Knip about a preload and a benchmark invoked outside the static import graph.

The parent of #167968 already had both file-write RPCs, and its identity cache fetched fresh data on the next refresh after the 60-second TTL expired. The prior test assertions covered avatar revalidation without an event, and #167968 changed them to require explicit invalidation while successful file writes still emitted no identity-change event.

The bridge already accepted a configured model and stopped forwarding silent frames before #152413 added model-specific handling for Gemini 3.8 Live, and that commit left the audio path intact. The PR's raw API probes show that the existing cutoff completed turns on Gemini 3.1, while both 3.8 variants required continued trailing audio, so the newer provider behavior exposed the incompatibility. The silence policy predates the shallow history boundary, and the available offline history did not establish its original commit.

The outbox already used WebSocket connectivity to gate sends and paced retryable refusals before cooperative suspension existed. The suspension commit added a retryable gateway-suspending refusal on sockets that could stay connected, exposing the outbox's assumption that transport connectivity was enough to resume sending.

I checked that Dashboard already said to keep one-off visualizations inline before #139705 exposed pinned-only authoring to recovered Control UI turns without an inline client. That new use made the existing Dashboard guidance conflict with the recovered turn’s widget schema, and the later Visualize skill repeated the inline directive.

The parent revision already exercised a successful first chat turn against a fresh configured store in the Gateway product test, and earlier validation recorded successful child delivery on a same-store restart. I checked that #169622 introduced the retained authorization and that the fix extends the existing cold-store admission test to verify that authorization stays current after registration.

The Zen path history and introducing diff show that #121030 added Kimi K3 with Max-only metadata and a test that expected Off to omit `reasoning_effort`. The fix PR's live comparison found that omission produced reasoning and explicit `none` disabled it, matching the payload behavior in the original implementation.

In the parent of #109709, steering was already the default, the embedded runner handled retries, and a failed request that did not require a compaction retry could settle even with queued input. The diff for #109709 added a queue check that continued the session before the runner could handle the failure. The later #110174 change preserved that behavior when it converted the return value from a boolean to a named action.

I checked the parent of #139997 and found that the eager native resolver already passed through the same slash-normalized Jiti targets as the on-demand resolver. The #145947 diff introduced the Bun SDK alias hook and passed those targets through from its first implementation.

The introducing diff already reused an open PR after pushing a new request’s commit, leaving the original request marker in the PR body. After an interruption and closure, that same diff ignored the accepted update’s closed PR and could create a replacement. I checked that the later repository backend carried forward the same lookup and creation fallback, while the guest-original-PR feature added a separate path for explicitly bound PRs.

I checked the introducing diff and its parent: the parent detected the package manager before the metadata check and printed the refusal directly to stderr. The structured metadata refusal reported known package installs as `unknown` from its first version, and the same mapping was still present immediately before the fix. The underlying metadata failure in the original report remains unidentified.

I checked the introducing diff and its parent: before #165607, a matching candidate with an unchanged lease was routed back to pending recovery, and #165607 introduced verified settlement while excluding `prepared` records. A later diff added `publication-complete` while preserving that exclusion, so the prepared case had been missing since verified settlement shipped.

I checked the introducing diff and the later ingress refactor. PR #110864 introduced deferred replay settlement and ended ingress tracking at transport adoption, before the logical replay writes finished, and the refactor preserved that boundary. The five-minute queue timeout was already in place when durable ingress shipped, so a handler could also outlive its ordering slot from the start.

PR #166519 introduced watermark reuse for entry replacement receipts with the process-wide guard already in place, so an unrelated transcript notification could force a fresh read from the first release of that path. I checked that the counter was already shared across sessions in the parent and that #167875 later made combined receipts advance the same counter before entry receipt readers consumed it. The fix adds coverage for both cases and reports fewer worker reads.

The commit that introduced the Side chat composer already disabled its question input while an answer was pending. I checked the later turn-history refactor and confirmed that it carried the same restriction forward using the new pending-turn state.

The July 11 diff shows that the existing poller already compared its deadline against Date.now() and used setTimeout for poll delays, so it was already sensitive to clock jumps. The July 16 change reused that deadline to cap individual requests. The offline history stops before July 1, so I could not verify whether the wall-clock deadline shipped with the original poller or replaced an earlier implementation.

The palette catalog search shipped with the failing comparison, so its introducing commit is the representative cause for this bundled fix. Signal alias search independently shipped with the same omission in #95738, whose first implementation used `!alias.includes(query)`. The Codex comparison predates the shallow boundary, and the available offline history did not establish its introducing commit.

I checked the introducing diff and its removed code, which show that Linux worker provisioning previously used the configured executable directly without a mandatory version probe. The live trace reported in the fix PR showed that a healthy 6.922-second probe selected managed 0.56 in place of configured 0.64. The remote-command reductions are performance improvements alongside that regression fix.

PR #146361 added a comparison against the pre-recovery payload, which lets an already-present explicit target pass even when the preview has a different target. Its parent and the July 1 snapshot already reused text previews without checking the final target, and the July 1 docs already described explicit reply tags. The offline history search stopped at a missing parent, so I could not identify the introducing commit or verify that this combination ever worked on main.

The grouped renderer already fell back to `userLabel ?? resolvedUserName` before the Control UI architecture refactor, and Markdown export already used “You” before the export commits in the blame candidates. The chat fallback was present at the July 1 history boundary, and the offline history lookup could not recover its introduction. The available diffs also did not establish a later change that first exposed the false attribution.

I checked #158489 and its parent: the old Gateway path parsed the complete buffer whenever it projected changed live text, and #158489 introduced an incremental projector that retained that work after a prose marker. Path history shows that #183198 moved the same condition into the stream module. The fix reduced measured parser work while delivering byte-identical text, and the reported timings did not establish a user-visible slowdown.

I checked the refactor's parent and confirmed that Copilot already sent the same public identity through model defaults and stream wrappers, while its auth hook returned only the API key and base URL. Core already registered auth output header values for exact-value redaction, so adding the public identity to that output caused the provider name to be masked.

The parent of #158703 already omitted provider attribution from stored native-auth bindings, normalized it on resume, and reused the stored value on warm turns. #158703 introduced the Ultrafast check with a guard that rejected that omitted value, and #160352 later added explicit Ultrafast selection while retaining the same provider argument.

The oldest available source already routes formatted Signal replies through a formatter that receives a size limit and table mode but no chunk mode, bypassing the plain-text chunking path. The July outbound recovery change preserved that routing, and the offline history lookup stopped at a missing parent, so I could not verify when the bypass was introduced or whether newline chunking had previously worked for those replies.

The parent had a rich-block renderer but no `<details>` mapping, and the introducing diff added both uncapped recursion in `unwrapUnclosed` and recursive rendering of nested details bodies. The later Markdown-inside-details rewrite changed the recursive rendering path and still imposed no bound before rendering, so the overflow was possible from the first version of the feature.

PR #103769 introduced automatic utility selection and sent the derived Anthropic model through a completion path that required provider credentials, even though the primary could already use a model-scoped CLI runtime. I checked the pre-introduction selection and PR #135711, which later routed utility calls through the selected model's runtime but left the automatic selection without the primary model's pin.

Before #163381, foreground Gateway startup already propagated unexpected errors to the shared CLI formatter, which printed the redacted reason with debug mode off. I checked that call path in the parent and confirmed that #163381 added the early return that suppressed the reason. Later commits restored reasons for invalid config and update commands, leaving ordinary Gateway startup errors on the terse path.

I checked the ACP harness and catalog publisher in #156278 and its parent. The parent handled native inspection errors generically, and #156278 introduced a distinct native sign-in outcome while counting it as a refresh failure from its first publication.

Quick Chat already called the getter during permission setup before #113337, when the getter could return as soon as it found an XCTest bundle and skip any later bundle with a missing URL. The July change made that scan eager, and the fix reports reproducing a trap with a missing URL, but the failing run's bundle order is unknown, so I could not confirm that the older scan would have returned before reaching that bundle.

In the causing commit's parent, the runner already supplied a synthetic group and sender, and the adapter used the chat opened for the scenario while accepting the supplied logical labels. The causing diff added participant and route validation while leaving that probe input in place, so a direct-message-only run rejected the group probe and other runs could reject its sender or logical conversation.
The PR documents an unused-export finding from Knip in scheduled CI. The commit diff confirms that only the export modifier changed, leaving the type, plugin API, and runtime behavior intact.

The original discount in #153545 covered long streams with the earlier frame shape, and the intervening OpenClaw diffs preserved its metadata check. Captures from Claude Code 2.1.296 and 2.1.310 show `api_message_id` on every stream event, which makes those deltas count as ordinary lines under the existing allowlist.

I checked the causing commit’s parent, where the mobile drawer already existed and an end-to-end test verified that the first Escape closed a nested session menu while leaving the drawer open. The draggable-drawer commit added an asynchronous import whose completion could refocus an already-open drawer after the user had entered a nested menu.

The introducing diff added the normalized results contract and wired it into the registered web search tool in the same commit. The original regex checked the shape of the date alone, and the affected file's history shows that the publication filter was unchanged until this fix.

I checked the causing commit's parent and confirmed that the relay already passed its environment to the anchor, which already acquired Linux subreaper ownership. The previous guard checked the module filename for a TypeScript extension, so a built JavaScript helper passed even with an empty instrumentation preload. The new guard rejected that same helper before it could acquire kernel ownership.

I checked the reader before July’s short-read fix and found that it already sampled file size before opening the file and assigned `cursor = size` even when the read returned fewer bytes. The August blame candidate preserved that behavior for newline-terminated reads. The available path history stops at the July 1 shallow boundary because an older object is missing, so I could not verify when the defect was introduced.

The parent already supported direct Codex plugin selection, and its CLI loaded the provider through the plugin registry, where Codex registration set the root required for inventory discovery. The causing diff routed the same command through a lightweight artifact that only re-exported the provider builder, leaving the root unset in a fresh process.

The path history and introducing diff show that moving project registry removal to the state worker added the admission protocol and its five-second worker deadline together. From the first version, a delayed host could lose the chance to grant a valid request because the worker had already changed its state from pending to refused.

The SQLite rollout introduced both the unguarded import and unconditional recovery report generation for an incomplete journal. I checked that batching preserved the exception path and that the later zero-issue guard separately suppressed reports for failures that had been recorded.

I checked the widget introduction and confirmed that Gateway reconfiguration already existed, disconnect handling retained the reply, and the renderer rebuilt its widgets using the newly connected Gateway’s Canvas URL. The introducing diff also chained layout updates while native work was pending, and the fix’s parent still had both behaviors despite the intervening recovery change adding Gateway checks for chat events.

The original ask_user registration checked session eligibility and tool policy and explicitly relied on a plain-text fallback across channels. I checked the later commits that added WhatsApp reaction handling and Mattermost buttons, but the local evidence does not establish whether the reported delivery failures existed at launch or began with a later code change.

The introducing diff added inline dictation with the premature Listening transition and no transcription phase, so the misleading feedback shipped with the feature. The path history shows that the ignored readiness and end-of-speech handlers originated in that commit, and the fix's controller test explicitly requires readiness before Listening. The cited cause accounts for the dictation defect, while attachment progress is a separate change in the same fix.

GitHub Copilot already used transient carriers for Claude Fable 5.1, whose model identity makes the new predicate return true. Both request builders previously allowed transient carriers to anchor the cache, and the model-based eligibility check introduced in #140621 still allowed them for this setup from its first version.

I checked the worker migration against its parent and confirmed that compound turns gained both worker execution and unconditional host imports in the same commit. The fix removes several additional import paths, and the reported heap measurements do not isolate the cost of the original loader.
